findings.desc: experiments/role-prompt-ab-replay/lib/replay.mjs:301-305 and protocol.json:14-23 — The two A/B arms are not pinned legacy/modular role-prompt bytes or a verified prompt-envelope reconstruction; armPrompt synthesizes one short label sentence per arm. `node experiments/role-prompt-ab-replay/run.mjs --json` therefore reports 1279 vs 1292 bytes for critical-01, measuring the labels plus shared JSON rather than either real role contract. This can validate harness determinism but cannot constitute a role-prompt A/B assembled-input measurement. Bind each arm to exact committed prompt/envelope bytes plus digest/contract version, or classify the arm metric itself INCONCLUSIVE and rename the artifact as a framework selfcheck.
findings.resolvedReason: Fixed in e36af72f74: canonical arms no longer synthesize placeholder prompt bytes; missing historical snapshots return PROMPT_SNAPSHOT_UNAVAILABLE and no prompt savings claim. Hermetic bytes are isolated selfcheck-only.

findings.desc: experiments/role-prompt-ab-replay/corpus.json:81-83,123-125,165-167,207-209 and lib/replay.mjs:308-320 — finding recall is marked EVALUABLE solely by replaying caller-authored `observedFindingsByArm`; those arm observations carry no source artifact, transcript/reviewer-run reference, evidence digest, or independent adjudication binding. The oracle `adjudication.evidenceRef` only supports that the seeded defect is valid, not that arm A or B actually detected it. `selfcheck.mjs` then prints `Recall: EVALUABLE` while merely checking schema/digests. Treat unbound arm outcomes exactly like unbound provider usage: reject numeric/detected observations or return INCONCLUSIVE until every arm observation is mechanically bound to immutable review output and independently adjudicated matching evidence.
findings.resolvedReason: Fixed in e36af72f74 and 6cf3fc7c47: caller/corpus observed findings were removed; canonical finding outputs remain unavailable and recall stays INCONCLUSIVE. Two real signed historical finding identities are bound without pretending they are replay outputs.

findings.desc: .lattice/story/actives/B-8d4b/checklist.json:7-10 marks lattice-experiment-protocol.md as a governing relatedDoc, but that document at lines 184-188 has an explicit Build gate requiring the S3 harness to implement rev3.1 exactly (five A1-A4 arms including provider-backed spend matching, 20-24 tasks, injections, GLMM/FDR). The delivered two-arm offline historical-observation replay intentionally does none of those things. This leaves two incompatible experiment contracts presented as simultaneously authoritative. Either remove this unrelated protocol from CHK-001/plan and state it governs a different experiment, or amend the protocol/canonical cross-reference so the authority boundary is unambiguous before declaring Story 3 delivered.

experiments/role-prompt-ab-replay/README.md:14-22 labels the ledger target as runtime output and documents a command that writes runtime/operator-run.jsonl, but experiments/role-prompt-ab-replay/runtime/ is not gitignored (git check-ignore returns no match). The documented command therefore leaves a clean Story worktree with an untracked 72-row ledger until the operator manually deletes it. Add an experiment-local ignore rule or document an ignored/temp output path so the runnable instructions do not create accidental repository artifacts.

experiments/role-prompt-ab-replay/lib/replay.mjs:135-179,308-320 and experiments/role-prompt-ab-replay/corpus.json:93-143 — HIGH: finding recall is marked EVALUABLE from corpus-authored observedFindingsByArm rows, but neither those rows nor adjudication.evidenceRef are bound to a verified output/evidence digest; validation only checks nonblank strings, and two machine evidenceRefs name files that do not exist. Because README says no model dispatch occurs, the harness can self-populate both arms as detecting every oracle and then self-report Recall: EVALUABLE. This violates the fail-closed/independent-adjudication intent; unbound observations must be INCONCLUSIVE or carry mechanically verified result/adjudication artifacts and digests.

experiments/role-prompt-ab-replay/lib/replay.mjs:301-305 and experiments/role-prompt-ab-replay/selfcheck.mjs:255 — MEDIUM: armPrompt hard-codes contract bytes from arm.id instead of arm.promptContract, and selfcheck has no contract-drift assertion. Independent probe changed A.promptContract legacy-full-context.v1→v999: experimentId changed but promptDigestChanged=false and bytesChanged=false. Thus verificationIntent replay-order-path-and-repeat-invariance and its recorded note claim contract drift coverage that does not exist. Assemble bytes from the pinned contract field (or reject unsupported contracts) and add a focused regression.

experiments/role-prompt-ab-replay/lib/replay.mjs:301-305,362 — HIGH: armPrompt ignores the frozen arm.promptContract value and hard-codes bytes solely from arm id. Repro: mutate protocol.arms[0].promptContract from legacy-full-context.v1 to .v2; experimentId and emitted metadata change but the A-arm promptDigest remains identical. This breaks the promised contract-drift sensitivity and can label old prompt bytes as a new contract.

experiments/role-prompt-ab-replay/lib/ledger.mjs:280-294 — HIGH: appendLedgerRecord performs read/verify/derive/append without a lock or compare-and-append primitive. A Promise.all of two valid first-record appends both fulfills with previousRecordHash=null, then readLedger fails LEDGER_CHAIN_BROKEN. Concurrent experiment writers can therefore corrupt the append-only ledger despite both calls succeeding.

experiments/role-prompt-ab-replay/lib/ledger.mjs:228-257 — MEDIUM: verifyLedgerRows validates only namespace/chain/order and never revalidates the canonical record schema, forbidden privacy fields, recordId, digests, usage, or disposition. A row augmented with rawPrompt=SECRET and a recomputed public recordHash is accepted. readLedger/analyze therefore admit manually injected private or malformed rows even though makeLedgerRecord rejects them.

experiments/role-prompt-ab-replay/lib/ledger.mjs:280-293 — MEDIUM: ledger path confinement has a check/use race. The code lstat-checks components, creates the directory, checks again, then opens by pathname with appendFile; a target or parent can be replaced by a symlink between the second check and open. Static symlink selfchecks do not cover this TOCTOU, so the claimed experiment-only write boundary is not mechanically guaranteed.
